Say you live in the US but VPN into the Netherlands while using a website based in Japan. Which country's laws apply? If you do something illegal in the Netherlands or Japan, do you have to be extradited to the Netherlands or Japan before you can be charged in this case?
Does using a VPNining into or using a website in another country nullify your country's laws?

Correct me if I'm wrong about this but for your example (TL;DR - what matters most is what country has to investigate the offense and how they cooperate on the investigation, not what country you were "using the internet in."):

possession offenses (e.g. you have child porn on your computer) - only US law applies to you because your computer is in the US

distribution offenses (e.g. upload said child porn to the Japanese website via the Dutch VPN) - you are liable under both Dutch and American law (the de facto rule being if your actions are illegal in both countries) while the website would be liable under Japanese law. Most likely the Dutch authorities would investigate and shut down your VPN server and you would go to court in the US to face punishment under US law I imagine. But in that case it would be up to the Dutch authorities to start this process so if what you are doing is legal in the Netherlands but not the US you might be ok when push comes to shove despite having violated US law on paper. The US authorities probably won't be able to decrypt your VPN stream or get directly to your VPN server for investigative purposes without the cooperation of the Dutch government. If your action is legal in the US but not the Netherlands than your VPN server could be shut down but not much more than that.

An online community you run victim of someone who isn't you posting illegal content (e.g. someone posts child porn to a Voat subverse) - the website, hosted in Japan, could be liable under Japanese law but as the community admin you likely aren't liable at all unless you openly allow or participate in sharing of illegal content or if you own the server.
